reply_text:
I found it: futon3c PR #68. I'm now checking how it fits with the 象-off switch from earlier.㊥ (PR #68) The work is futon3c PR #68, "Port M-象-2000 frontend to JVM and TypeScript (P23)". It was built in a cloud Claude session on branch `claude/modest-newton-p7guja` and merged on 2026-10-02 as `cb6090af`. It is already on local master. It moves the 象 turn pipeline (recording, sending turns to the 象 seats, collecting the readings) out of Emacs and Python into the JVM. It adds routes under `/api/alpha/xiang/turns`, plus a TypeScript client and widget in `packages/xiang-client/` for Element and Matrix. What should I do with it?

㊢ (what else landed) Three commits since the merge build on it:
- **`1b926e00`:** adds the 小象 draft tier, a classical pre-parse that is handed to 象. This may be the "limited extension" you mean.
- **`b7f02576`:** records the bridge agents' replies without sending them to 象.
- **`b2d41946`:** stops the JVM from sending turns that weren't asked for analysis.

The write-up, including what the cloud session could and couldn't test, is in `holes/labs/M-象-2000/P23-frontend-port.md`. It had no JVM, futon1b or Emacs to test against.

㊩ (the 象-off from earlier) This affects what I told you last turn. `象-off` only stops the Emacs path. The JVM now sends turns to 象-1 to 象-4 by itself, and it has no off switch. Turns that come in through the Matrix bridge with immediate dispatch will still reach the seats while 象 is "off". The JVM's health route shows it in use: its last reading (`turn-0flV3D`) was at about 05:14 UTC, shortly before I switched 象 off.

🈸 (two options) 
1. I could add an off/on switch to the JVM's turn service that also takes a written re-arm condition, and have `象-off` / `象-on` set it too, so one command stops both paths.
2. I could review PR #68 and the follow-up commits.

Which do you want, or both?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (how they work) `M-x 象-off` asks "Re-arm 象 when:" and won't accept an empty answer, following the war-room pattern card wr-26. It sets the analysis policy to `never` and keeps the previous policy. It also writes the condition, with a timestamp, to `~/.emacs-graph/session-turn-analysis/xiang-off.log`. `M-x 象-on` puts the previous policy back and logs that too. Running `象-off` twice only replaces the written condition, so `象-on` still goes back to the policy from before the first `象-off`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(testing) I tested them in a separate batch Emacs, so your live setting wasn't touched:
- An empty condition is refused.
- The policy goes off and back to the one it had before (`unmatched` in the test).
- A second `象-on` just says 象 isn't off.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (limits) The seats stay registered with Agency. As you didn't ask for deregistration, I left it out. The off state lasts only for this Emacs session, so a restart turns 象 back on.
